chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said:
Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: Do not perform sajdah except upon the earth or that which the earth grows, except cotton and linen.

key_terms.أَنْبَتَتْهُ: that which it causes to grow, referring to vegetation produced from the earth
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth or ground, the primary valid surface for sajdah
key_terms.الْقُطْنَ: cotton, an excluded material for sajdah here
key_terms.الْكَتَّانَ: linen, an excluded material for sajdah here
key_terms.تَسْجُدْ: to perform sajdah, meaning to prostrate in worship

ai.seo_question: What materials are permissible for sajdah in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the validity of sajdah, restricting it to earth and what grows from the earth, while excluding cotton and linen. It is significant in Shia fiqh as a foundational text for the laws of prostration in salat (prayer).
